key_insight: Adaptive shot allocation can reduce quantum debugging executions by focusing measurements on uncertain assertions while maintaining comparable confidence.
engineering_relevance: Allocating shots across mid-circuit assertions can make statistical debugging more resource-efficient as quantum programs scale.
method: Implement four allocation strategies in the CUDA-Q-based QDB debugger.
Compare equal split, static weight allocation, adaptive entropy routing, and sequential retirement.
Use repeated circuit executions and statistical hypothesis tests to check expected qubit-state characteristics.
evidence_signal: Evaluations across multiple circuits under noise-free and depolarizing-noise conditions report substantially lower total shot usage with adaptive strategies, though the abstract provides no numerical savings.
watch_item: Benefits under broader hardware noise models and on physical quantum devices are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Shot Allocation Strategies in Debugging Quantum Circuits
